source: Do more to orchestrate your agents, especially toward more architectured/systemitized code, better durable tooling for doing what they're working on

if you start to understand the software as essentially stratified layers of API, with the internal hull being the pure transformation functions and the external kernel being the effectful ones [...] you will do more good work to condense our codebase into a maintainable size and shape

norms.statement: Every import edge stays inside the house's layered DAG (data/records/house-layers.json): the target layer must be named in the source layer's own `imports` allow-list, or be the source layer itself, rather than merely sitting at or below some numeric rank.

A house-scoped specifier names an existing house package and a subpath that package's own `exports` (or, lacking `exports`, the file itself) actually resolves; a relative specifier resolves to a real file on disk.
An import is a Node builtin, a relative path, or a house scope -- never a third-party package; a house scope owns a capability instead of merely passing an external one through.

House source is plain Node: a .ts/.mts/.cts file that is not a .d.* declaration is a deviation from standard package shape, and (for a change under gate) an offense on its own. Plain Node only, no TypeScript, node:test for tests.

The internal hull is the pure transformation functions and the external kernel is the effectful ones; a hull module may not reach a kernel module by a relative import, because doing so makes its own purity depend on that effect. A module classifies kernel only by a direct effect marker in its own text (an effectful import, a process stream read, fetch(, Date.now(/new Date(), Math.random(, or a named node:crypto randomness call) -- never by what it composes -- so this finding fires only for a direct hull-to-kernel relative import; the census's `reaches` (shortest relative-import hop count to a kernel module, within the module's own package) and the informational `hullReachingKernel` count (hull modules with reaches >= 2) report a module's transitive distance from an effect without moving the norm.

A module earns its place by defining something; one whose statements are all `export * from` or `export {...} from` forwards without transforming and should be condensed away or folded into its consumer.
A package ships its source, not a compiled twin: a checked-in dist/ directory beside the manifest is a deviation.
One codebase, no per-package node_modules and no package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or yarn.lock checked in beside the manifest.
Every exact (non-`*`) target named in a package.json `exports` map resolves to a file that actually exists on disk.

A house-scoped package imported under a package's own src/scripts is declared in its `dependencies`, and every house-scoped `dependencies` entry is actually imported somewhere in the package; the manifest's stated dependency closure and the code's real one match in both directions.

Condensing the codebase into a maintainable size and shape means one implementation per capability across the house, not a SignCell-and-a-SignChain-and-a-SignGraph plurality of near-duplicates for the same job; no tool yet audits this.
